narrative: OMX30 faces a mixed setup on Friday morning. While global risk appetite showed strength overnight (NASDAQ +1.69%, Nikkei +1.38%), European bourses retreated 0.64–0.68%, creating crosscurrents. The sharp 118bp decline in US 10Y yields is a double-edged sword: it supports valuations and should benefit defensive/dividend stocks (banks on wider NIM, pharma on risk rotation), but pressures growth narratives and tech sentiment. Oil's 5.7% plunge cuts input-cost risk for industrials but hints at growth anxiety. With RSI at 46.8 (neutral) and MACD below signal, the index lacks directional conviction despite sitting +6.1% above the 200-MA. The +7.9% ROC-90 shows underlying momentum, but ADX at 21.5 with bearish DI bias suggests volatility may persist. Key watch: can OMX30 hold the 50-MA (3180) support given the yield-driven headwinds?
morningBrief: OMX30 opens Friday in a choppy backdrop. US equity strength (+1.4% S&P avg) is being offset by European weakness and a sharp yield selloff (US 10Y -118bp), which typically compresses growth multiples. Technically, the index remains in a bull structure (+6.1% above 200-MA at ~3085) but sits neutral at RSI 46.8 with MACD below signal—no clear directional edge. Sector rotations likely: banks should catch a bid (NIM expansion on yields), while industrials may face headwinds despite lower oil (sentiment risk). Copper +0.87% is a green light for Boliden; the oil crash (-5.72%) eases input costs for Volvo/Atlas Copco but watch for demand signals. Key level: 50-MA at 3180 is immediate resistance; break below 3085 (lower Bollinger) signals weakness. US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET is the main trigger—any shock could break the current gridlock. Lean defensive (AstraZeneca, Essity, SEB) in the absence of conviction.
